rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 0 line 5 "The four composition mechanisms this page names are the move." forward-references content only elaborated in chunk 2's Layer 3. Stays inside because it is a full noun phrase previewing the page's OWN structure ("this page names"), not a pronoun/demonstrative standing in for an already-established referent -- unlike the rule's own violation example ("before the three things get named"), it does not ask the reader to already be tracking a specific unnamed antecedent, only forecasts the page's shape (ordinary abstract/TL;DR rhetoric). Rest of the deck: every later pronoun/demonstrative resolves within its own chunk or against a same-file earlier chunk (e.g. chunk 8 line 165 "Dino's four mechanisms" reuses chunk 2's Layer 3 naming; chunk 6 line 131 "this doc" is self-referential and trivially resolvable; chunk 7 line 157 "the slash command" resolves to the immediately preceding clause in the same bullet). No never-named, vague-with-history, or re-chunk-stranded referent found.

grep of the body for callback-style phrasing ("the opening lecture", "earlier module", "as covered", "said") returns nothing; this is a standalone supplementary page with no other-file narrative callbacks at all. Closest line: chunk 6 line 131 "Companion diagrams ship with this doc." names the artifact directly ("this doc") rather than locating it by position -- passes cleanly.

`node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file <path> --report`: every one of the 8 `##` chunks carries 75-321 words and 0-19 bullets of substantive content (TL;DR, the smallest, is a full 75-word paragraph). No chunk is a single wait-state or context-dependent bullet.

Checked all 8 headers against their chunk content: "## The three-layer model" (line 15) is organized under exactly three `### Layer 1/2/3` subheadings; "## Skill catalog by phase" (line 67) lists skills grouped under 5 phase subheadings; "## Diagrams" (line 129) literally embeds 3 diagrams; "## Map your own kit" (line 163) is the imperative worksheet its body walks through. Every header is a true summary of its own chunk; none is contradicted by its content.

Per sub-item, mechanical + manual: (1) "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction: `grep -niE 'not [a-z].*\. not [a-z]'` -> 0 hits. (2) anaphora/epistrophe triples: `grep -niE '\bevery [a-z]+ [a-z]+\b.*\bevery [a-z]+ [a-z]+\b'` -> 0 hits; the three "### Layer 1/2/3" and five phase subheadings are structural labels, not a repeated-phrase-initial prose tic. (3) self-grading superlatives: `grep -niE '\b(most|best|greatest|unmatched|unparalleled|revolutionary|game-chang)\w*\b'` -> 0 hits; line 155 "Unusually high analysis-to-action ratio" describes DINO's architecture, not this training's own value, so it is not a value-prop-leak superlative. (4) number + own retraction: none present -- every count (four mechanisms, three layers, seven principles) is stated flatly with no hedge/retraction. (5) abstraction-noun stacks: closest is line 155's "analysis-to-action ratio", a precise engineering metric name rather than vague jargon -- stays inside. (6) verb triplets with an empty leg: none found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -niE '\b(surface|firing|compendium|forcing function|\bbeat\b|\bmood\b|connections)\b'` against the body: 2 hits, both "surface map" / "access-surface map" (lines 44, 74), describing what `/access-control-analysis` and `/stride` produce. This is the ordinary security-engineering term (attack/access surface), not our repo-internal "surface"-as-noun dialect -- context is unambiguously security threat-modeling, exactly the carve-out for ordinary engineering usage. No `compendium`, `firing`, `forcing function`, `beat`, or `mood` anywhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Four bold clusters checked: (a) chunk 1 line 11 (TL;DR) bolds all four composition-mechanism names in one paragraph -- this is exactly "a law/consolidation slide may carry one handle per law": each handle is <=5 words and the slide's whole job is naming the file's four core mechanisms. (b) chunk 2's Layer-2 axis table (lines 26-31, `**Scope**`/`**Phase**`/`**Posture**`/`**Enforcement**`) and chunk 2's Layer-3 mechanism list (line 42 etc., `**1. Explicit load.**`...`**4. Hand-off pipeline.**`) are structural table/list row-labels naming coined taxonomy terms, one handle per row -- same consolidation-slide logic as (a). (c) chunk 4's Workflow-shapes table (lines 106-111, `**A * Standard feature**` etc.) is the same structural row-label pattern. (d) chunk 5 "Design principles" (lines 119-125): every one of 7 numbered entries opens with a bolded FULL sentence (5-7 words, e.g. line 119 "**A skill never duplicates another's logic.**") rather than a short handle -- this is the file's closest approach to the classic violation shape. But `skill-stacking.md` lives under `supplementary/`, and this section's entries are paragraphs (bold lead sentence + prose explanation, bold never crossing the first-sentence boundary) -- exactly the named carve-out "on a prose-paragraph lookup page, the bolded lead sentence IS the handle... the ~5-word cap yields to one full lead sentence per entry." Design principles is a scan-to-find-the-row reference list on a supplementary page, matching that shape. Chunk 3's `**mandatory on ...**` qualifiers and chunk 7's bullet leads (lines 155-159) are all independently <=5 words, no carve-out needed there.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 7 line 156 "`/ship` is the only orchestrator... justified by absorbing four end-of-workflow commands into one verb" echoes chunk 1 line 11's "`/ship`... absorbs the closing commands of every workflow... into one user-typed verb." Stays inside because chunk 7's bullet does new work with the fact: it is the JUSTIFICATION for a new, distinct claim (`/ship` is the corpus's only orchestrator, a deliberate architectural exception) rather than a bare re-announcement. No self-referential design-commentary/predicate-leak found (line 5's "read for the patterns, not for copying" is scope-setting for a worked example, not the curriculum narrating its own pedagogy). No aphorism kicker restating its own header: chunk 8's closing line 172 "Naming the shape now makes the next skill's place obvious" adds a reason (future clarity), it does not just restate "map your own kit."

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule 15's imperative/declarative mood split is defined for exercise vs. lecture files specifically ('Exercise `##` headings = imperative... Lecture headings = claims'). This file is a supplementary reference/progressive-reading page, not an exercise or lecture, so the binary mood contract doesn't bind it the same way; headings here are a mix of topical labels ('Diagrams', 'Skill catalog by phase') and one imperative worksheet heading ('Map your own kit'), consistent with a lookup/reference register rather than a violation of either mood. None of the diff's wording changes touched a `##` header itself.
